candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar's campaign against Jerusalem in Jehoiakim's third year; temple vessels taken to Shinar
candidates.description: In the third year of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it; Jehoiakim was given into his hand with some temple vessels, which were carried to the land of Shinar and put in the treasure house of his god.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah

ambiguities: "Third year" vs Jeremiah's "fourth year" (Jer 25:1; 46:2): regnal-reckoning question.
No Babylonian source names Jerusalem before 597.

candidates.title: Selection, renaming and training of young Judean nobles for the Babylonian court
candidates.description: The king ordered Ashpenaz to bring in royal and noble Israelite youths to be taught the learning and language of the Chaldeans for three years with provisions from the king's table; Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah received Babylonian names.
ambiguities: Whether "eunuchs" (sārîs) denotes castration or court officials generally.

candidates.title: Daniel's refusal of the king's food and the ten-day test
candidates.description: Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the king's food and wine; the steward tested the four on vegetables and water for ten days, after which they looked healthier, and their rations were changed.
ambiguities: The narrative states divine favour (1:9); not testable historically.

candidates.title: The youths' wisdom and their presentation before Nebuchadnezzar
candidates.description: God gave the four knowledge and wisdom, Daniel understanding of visions and dreams; at the end of the appointed time they were presented to the king, who found them ten times better than his magicians and enchanters.

temporal_statements.phrase: At the end of the days which the king had appointed

ambiguities: Relation of the three-year training to "the second year of Nebuchadnezzar" in Dan 2:1.

candidates.title: Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus
candidates.description: A closing note that Daniel continued until the first year of Cyrus.

temporal_statements.phrase: even to the first year of King Cyrus

ambiguities: "Continued" (at court? in life?) — Dan 10:1 dates a later vision to Cyrus's third year. To be researched with Dan 5–6 (fall of Babylon, Cyrus).

verse_coverage.notes: Language switch: the narrative continues in Aramaic from the second half of this verse to 7:28.

candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar's troubling dream and the decree against the wise men
candidates.description: In his second year Nebuchadnezzar demanded that his diviners tell him both his dream and its meaning; when they could not, he decreed the death of Babylon's wise men, including Daniel and his companions, whom Arioch went to execute.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar

ambiguities: "Second year" vs the three-year training (1:5, 18).
The text switches from Hebrew to Aramaic at 2:4b ("in the Syrian language") and stays in Aramaic to 7:28.

candidates.title: The secret revealed to Daniel and his interpretation before the king
candidates.description: Daniel and his companions prayed; the secret was revealed to Daniel in a night vision; Arioch brought him to the king, and Daniel attributed the revelation to the God of heaven.

candidates.title: The statue of four metals and the stone (dream content)
candidates.description: The dream image as recounted by Daniel.
ambiguities: Symbolic content — not a historical occurrence.

candidates.title: The four kingdoms and the everlasting kingdom (interpretation)
candidates.description: Daniel's interpretation of the image as a sequence of kingdoms followed by God's everlasting kingdom.

temporal_statements.phrase: In the days of those kings

ambiguities: Only the head of gold is identified in the text.

candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar honours Daniel and appoints him over the province of Babylon
candidates.description: The king prostrated himself, confessed Daniel's God, made Daniel ruler over the province of Babylon and chief over the wise men, and appointed his three companions over the province's affairs.

verse_coverage.notes: Greek Daniel inserts the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Young Men after this verse (non-canonical; indexed as a document).
The Aramaic text continues with 3:31–33, which English Bibles number 4:1–3.

candidates.title: The golden image and its dedication on the plain of Dura
candidates.description: Nebuchadnezzar set up a gold image 60 by 6 cubits on the plain of Dura and summoned the officials of the provinces to its dedication; at the sound of the instruments all peoples were to fall down and worship, on pain of the furnace.
ambiguities: No date in the Aramaic text; Brenton's Septuagint reads "in his eighteenth year".
Instrument names include Greek loanwords.

candidates.title: Accusation of the three Jews and their refusal
candidates.description: Chaldeans accused Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego of not serving the king's gods; summoned, they refused to worship the image, trusting their God to deliver them or not.
ambiguities: Daniel is absent from the chapter.

candidates.title: The fiery furnace and the deliverance
candidates.description: The furnace was heated seven times hotter; the bound men were thrown in, the executioners died, the king saw four men walking unharmed in the fire, and the three came out without even the smell of fire.
ambiguities: Identity of the fourth figure (3:25; the king calls him an angel in 3:28). English versions differ: "a son of the gods" vs "the Son of God".
Greek Daniel inserts the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three after 3:23 (non-canonical; SPEC 5.6).

candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar's decree and the promotion of the three
candidates.description: The king blessed their God, decreed death for anyone speaking against him, and promoted the three in the province of Babylon.

candidates.title: Nebuchadnezzar's proclamation to all peoples (letter frame)
candidates.description: The chapter is framed as a royal letter in which the king praises the Most High.
ambiguities: In the Aramaic text these verses are 3:31–33.

candidates.title: The king's dream of the tree; Daniel summoned to interpret
candidates.description: At rest in his palace, the king dreamed and summoned his diviners, who failed; Daniel/Belteshazzar was called.

candidates.title: The great tree and the watcher's decree (dream content)
candidates.description: The dream image as recounted by the king.

temporal_statements.phrase: let seven times pass over him

ambiguities: Symbolic content.

candidates.title: Daniel's interpretation: the decree against the king
candidates.description: Daniel identifies the tree as the king and announces his humbling for seven times, urging repentance.

candidates.title: The boast over Babylon and the king's madness
candidates.description: Twelve months later the king boasted over the Babylon he had built; a voice from heaven announced the sentence and he was driven from men, living like an animal.

temporal_statements.phrase: At the end of twelve months

ambiguities: Proposed Nabonidus tradition behind the story.

candidates.title: Restoration and confession
candidates.description: At the end of the days the king's reason returned; he praised the Most High and was restored to his kingdom with added greatness.

temporal_statements.phrase: At the end of the days

candidates.title: Amos's prophetic words dated by the superscription
candidates.description: The superscription attributes the book to Amos, one of the herdsmen of Tekoa, and dates what he "saw" concerning Israel to the days of Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash of Israel.

temporal_statements.phrase: in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash

ambiguities: Whether the dating refers to a single vision occasion or a longer ministry.
Whether Uzziah's 'days' include his coregency years (model-dependent).

candidates.title: The earthquake in the days of Uzziah
candidates.description: The superscription places Amos's words "two years before the earthquake", referring to a known earthquake without further description.
ambiguities: Whether Zechariah 14:5 refers to the same earthquake (likely by wording; tested in Rule 04).
Whether "two years" is exact or counted inclusively.

candidates.title: The LORD roars from Zion
candidates.description: Poetic announcement that the LORD will roar from Zion, with pastures mourning and the top of Carmel withering.
ambiguities: Some interpreters connect the imagery to drought or to the earthquake; no such link is stated in the text.

candidates.title: Oracle against Damascus
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Damascus: fire on the house of Hazael and the palaces of Ben Hadad; the people of Aram to go into captivity to Kir.
ambiguities: 2 Kings 16:9 records Tiglath-pileser deporting Damascus to Kir — a proposed fulfillment to evaluate in Rule 04.

candidates.title: Damascus "threshed Gilead"
candidates.description: The oracle cites Aramean (Damascus) aggression against Gilead as the grounds for judgment.
ambiguities: Likely refers to Aramean campaigns of Hazael's era (cf. 2 Kgs 10:32–33); identification to be researched.

candidates.title: Oracle against Gaza and the Philistines
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron.

candidates.title: Gaza deported whole communities to Edom
candidates.description: The oracle cites Gaza carrying away whole communities to hand them over to Edom.
ambiguities: Specific occasion unidentified.

candidates.title: Oracle against Tyre
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Tyre.

candidates.title: Tyre delivered communities to Edom, breaking a "brotherly covenant"
candidates.description: The oracle cites Tyre delivering whole communities to Edom and not remembering a brotherly covenant.
ambiguities: The covenant referred to is not identified in the text.

candidates.title: Oracle against Edom
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Edom: fire on Teman and the palaces of Bozrah.

candidates.title: Edom pursued "his brother" with the sword
candidates.description: The oracle cites Edom pursuing his brother with the sword and unending anger.
ambiguities: "His brother" is commonly read as Israel/Judah; the specific conflict is unidentified.

candidates.title: Oracle against Ammon
candidates.description: Judgment oracle against Ammon: fire on the wall of Rabbah; its king and princes to go into captivity.

candidates.title: Ammon's atrocities in Gilead to enlarge its border
candidates.description: The oracle cites Ammonite atrocities against pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their border.
ambiguities: Specific campaign unidentified.
